name: Uflex Ltd
title: Uflex Ltd - 500148 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: UFlex Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 26% YoY to Rs.48,694 million, with normalized EBITDA up 95% to Rs.7,588 million at a 15.6% margin.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 26% YoY to Rs.48,694 million, adding Rs.10,084 million, and normalized EBITDA rose 95% to Rs.7,588 million with margin up 550 bps to 15.6%. Overseas operations drove most of the growth, contributing 74% of incremental normalized EBITDA. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of around 30% growth in revenue and EBITDA, noting H1 delivered about 49-51% of revenue and 60-62% of EBITDA targets. Leverage fell to 3.33x from above 4.5x, with a 3-3.5x year-end target.

financial_highlights.metric: Net profit after tax and NCI
Leverage (net debt to EBITDA, as stated)

segments.name: Overseas operations
segments.commentary: Contributed 56% of incremental revenue and 74% of incremental normalized EBITDA (Rs.3,694 million total incremental EBITDA). Key contributors were Egypt, Mexico, Hungary, USA, Poland and Nigeria.

segments.name: India operations
segments.commentary: Contributed 44% of incremental revenue and 26% of incremental normalized EBITDA. India packaging films and PET chips were cited as strong performers.

segments.name: Packaging films
segments.commentary: Volume up 3% YoY to 129,025 MT, helped by converters preferring local and regional producers.

segments.name: Packaging business (flexible/aseptic)
segments.commentary: Volume down 3.9% YoY to 34,507 MT, reflecting a shift toward higher-margin flexible packaging in India. Value-added products are about 30% of sales and targeted at 50% by FY29.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue and EBITDA growth guided at around 30%; management said it remains on track.
H2 FY27 sales volume growth expected to be in the same range as H1 (about 2%).
Leverage guided to 3-3.5x by end FY27; management expects lower leverage in FY28-FY29 as new capacity reaches full utilisation.
Capacity utilisation is about 80% now, with a target of at least 90% next year (FY28).
Value-added products targeted at 50% of top line by FY29.
Blended EBITDA margin of 14-15% described as sustainable, with a long-term aim to improve it.
Management said the goal is to at least double FY26 tonnage output by FY29 through utilisation, not to triple turnover.
capex_capacity: Q2 FY27 capex of Rs.5,689 million, mainly for the Egypt aseptic packaging facility, Noida Sector 155 recycling unit and Dharwad BOPP line.
Egypt aseptic plant (12 billion packs) to start commercial production in H2 FY27, likely before March 2027, with utilisation of about 30% in year one, 60% in year two and 100% in year three.
Dharwad BOPP line expected to start commercial operations in H1 FY28.
Noida Sector 155 recycling facility (39,600 MTPA) and Mexico WPP bag facility (80 million units) are ramping; Mexico running at about 30-35% utilisation.
Two coating lines in Egypt and Mexico are commissioning. CWIP closing balance is about Rs.2,000 crore by March 2027, most of which is expected to be capitalised by FY28.
India aseptic capacity is about 12 billion packs at about 80% utilisation.
demand_pricing: Plain BOPET film spread has ranged Rs.25-35/kg over nine months, per management; value-added and coated films carry higher spreads.
Plain BOPET film price moved from Rs.108 in January 2026 to Rs.151 by end-October 2026, tracking crude (about Rs.90s in January vs Rs.110-112 in Sep-Oct).
Recycled PET chips: film grade about Rs.114/kg and bottle grade Rs.128-130/kg, versus virgin chips at about Rs.115/kg.
Domestic margins are structurally below overseas margins because overseas realisations are higher; competition in Indian aseptic is intense, with cheap imports from Indonesia and others.
Management is shifting packaging focus toward large customers with higher margins, which lowers concentration risk.
Receivables are expected to fall by year-end FY27 as the one-to-two-month lag overlap eases.

qa_highlights.question: When will the company reduce its Rs.8,000 crore debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited leverage down to 3.33x from above 4.5x, a 3-3.5x target for FY27-end, and about Rs.1,000 crore of capex not yet commercialised. Leverage is expected to fall further when FY28-29 capacity reaches full utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why are margins rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to utilisation reaching about 80%, which spreads fixed costs, plus higher-margin overseas capacity near customers in Egypt, Nigeria and Mexico.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Egypt aseptic plant ramp-up and returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Commercial production is expected before March 2027, with 30%/60%/100% utilisation over three years. Management targets a 3-5 year payback and did not give segment margins or breakeven utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company give up packaging volume to focus on flexible packaging?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some volume may be lost in lower-margin products while revenue and margin rise. Surajit Pal said the focus is on large customers, which broadens the base and lowers concentration risk.

qa_highlights.question: How has the spread on BOPET film moved?
qa_highlights.answer: Plain BOPET spread ranged Rs.25-35/kg, with a consistent average over nine months, despite film prices moving sharply with crude. Pass-through contracts are cited as the reason.

qa_highlights.question: What is the blended margin and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended EBITDA margin is 14-15%, with overseas margins well above India. Management called it sustainable over the long term and said the aim is to improve it, not just hold it.

risks_watch: Leverage at 3.33x remains high versus the 3-3.5x year-end target; debt reduction depends on new capacity ramping up.
Egypt aseptic (30% year-one utilisation) and WPP Mexico (30-35%) ramp-up timing and customer approvals are unproven; management did not name customers.
Crude and raw-material volatility amid the West Asia conflict; film prices fell from Rs.151 in October, and management said Q3/Q4 spreads will be watched.
Indian aseptic margins are under pressure from cheap imports and competition.
Recycling utilisation is currently low, despite government recycled-content norms.
Management did not give volume guidance beyond H2 FY27 volume growth of about 2%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, margins and overseas expansion, with repeated references to the 30% FY27 target and H1 delivery. More cautious on leverage, and evasive on segment-level margins, Egypt returns and the tax reconciliation. Some answers were loosely worded, and the chair corrected a question on volume versus value growth.
key_quotes: We have brought down those leverage ratios from 4.5 plus to 3.33 in Q2 FY27.
Overseas operations remained the key growth engine, contributing 56% of incremental revenue and 70% of incremental normalized EBITDA.

adds.what: Egypt aseptic packaging plant (12 billion packs)
Mexico WPP bag facility (80 million units), ramping at 30-35% utilisation

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 revenue and EBITDA growth of around 30%, with H1 at about 49-51% of revenue and 60-62% of EBITDA targets; backing is partial, citing Egypt aseptic (12bn packs, H2 FY27 start, 30% utilisation yr1), Dharwad BOPP (H1 FY28) and value-added mix, but H1 volume growth is only about 2% and H2 is guided similar.

oneOffs.what: Net profit +689% YoY reflects a very weak year-ago profit base, not revenue; no one-off item named in brief

quality.why: Revenue rose 26% (Rs.10,084 million) while total volume grew only 1.5% and packaging films 3%, so growth is mainly price/realisation-driven (BOPET film prices rose from Rs.108 to Rs.151 with crude) plus overseas capacity additions, with the brief naming no explicit one-off items to strip out.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Normalized EBITDA margin rose 550 bps to 15.6% on utilisation near 80% and higher-margin overseas capacity, and management calls the 14-15% blended margin sustainable with a long-term aim to improve it.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Egypt aseptic plant (12 billion packs) is due to start commercial production in H2 FY27, likely before March 2027, and Dharwad BOPP line in H1 FY28; Q2 capex was Rs.5,689 million and CWIP heads toward about Rs.2,000 crore by March 2027.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 FY27 total volume grew only 1.5% YoY and H2 is guided to about 2%, with packaging volume down 3.9%; the growth comes from value and mix rather than tonnage.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 80% and management targets 90% next year, so with Egypt and Dharwad still ramping, new capex is likely to be needed once they fill.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 growth of around 30% was only reiterated, with H1 at about 49-51% of revenue and 60-62% of EBITDA targets, leaving no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 volume is guided to about 2% and film prices fell from Rs.151 in October amid crude volatility, while leverage at 3.33x sits above the 3-3.5x year-end target band's midpoint; the 30% target needs H2 delivery.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Value-added products are about 30% of sales and targeted at 50% by FY29, with Egypt aseptic and Dharwad BOPP coming on stream, though no specific new product names were given.

rows.label: Leverage to 3-3.5x by FY27-end
rows.why: Leverage fell to 3.33x from above 4.5x, and management guided a 3-3.5x year-end range, with further reduction expected in FY28-29 as new capacity fills.

rows.label: Overseas growth (Egypt, Mexico, Hungary, USA, Poland, Nigeria)
rows.why: Overseas delivered 56% of incremental revenue and 74% of incremental normalized EBITDA (Rs.3,694 million), and Mexico WPP is already ramping at 30-35% utilisation.

rows.label: Receivables fall by FY27-end
rows.why: Management expects receivables to decline as the one-to-two-month lag overlap eases, supporting cash flow toward the leverage target.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 30% FY27 growth target, margins and overseas expansion, but cautious on leverage and evasive on segment margins, Egypt returns and tax; analysts pressed on debt reduction, margin sustainability and volume versus value growth.
